claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and the rider wins by breaking any one. Limb (b) is broken here. The computed arrival block on the driver's own 93-fix trace returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0 across the whole 08:05:10 to 08:20:30 window: there is no run of in-radius, accuracy-qualified fixes anywhere in the trace, so the driver was not at the pickup point to the standard POL-NS-02 sets for a STANDARD zone (50 m radius, 25 m accuracy filter). EV-GPS-00212 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and its own admissibility note is explicit that poor horizontal accuracy here is data rather than a defect, and that the record simply cannot place the driver inside the geofence to the standard POL-NS-02 requires. That is a failure of the policy test, not an impairment discount. The $4.00 is not chargeable.

Independently of the geofence, the waiting period was never served. The free waiting period in force on this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 300 seconds, which governs over the 180 second default, and POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the driver's arrival tap. The measured effective dwell is 0 seconds (accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec 0.0 over run_count 0), a shortfall of 300 seconds on the policy's own arithmetic. Under POL-NS-06 that shortfall refunds the cancellation fee in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she answered messages.

The driver cannot bridge the shortfall by summing separate intervals, because POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits accumulation only where a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so limb (i) is simply unavailable and the shortfall stands at the full 300 seconds. I do not assert limb (i) against the missing artifact; I rely on the absence itself, which is citable, and the derived block records the same conclusion (advisory_missing).

The driver also cannot fall back on the platform-confirmed arrival route. POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO marker, and the marker in force on this trip is BUTTON - trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is 'BUTTON' - so the platform's arrival and wait-timer events cannot carry POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c). Because the arrival was driver-pressed, both his arrival and his dwell must be established from the exported trace under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05, and on that trace there is no qualifying in-radius fix and no qualifying stationary run.

The rider's refund does not depend on winning the 50 metre point. If the driver is treated as stationary near but not at the pin, POL-NS-03 still refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. His trace is not a kerbside wait: across the 15-minute window his fixes average 294.05 m from the pickup pin, reach 1082.40 m away, and record speeds up to 43.5 km/h over a 3.2 km trace, with run_count 0 of held position. So on either clause - POL-NS-02 or POL-NS-03 - the $4.00 goes back to the rider.

On the POL-NS-03 route the driver bears his own loss and receives nothing, under limb (i): the rider stated the correct entrance in the chat log - 'im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here' at 08:15:02 - and 'Exit A' is the registered pickup point itself, 'Raffles Place MRT (Exit A)'. The driver replied at 08:15:30 and then cancelled at 08:20:30 without moving to her. Where the rider named the entrance and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, no compensation is payable.

The pin-ambiguity goodwill also fails on its own terms. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) requires both that neither party specified a sub-location and that trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2 or more. registered_pickup_points is 1, and the rider did specify a sub-location, so limb (ii) cannot be reached and the 50 percent goodwill is not available.

I concede that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and I do not run it as her route to the fee. Limb (a) is satisfied: her 08:15:02 message is locating on its face. But limb (b) fails, because the driver replied in the chat 28 seconds later at 08:15:30, which takes the case out of the clause regardless of what the reply said. The same message still does work under POL-NS-03(i): it shows she told him exactly where she was standing, and he cancelled anyway.

The rider's own device corroborates her account of standing at the kerb. Her track holds 60 fixes between 08:08:00 and 08:22:00, every one of them at 0.0 km/h, at distances of 2.18 m to 40.37 m from the pickup pin - inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius on the raw numbers. I do not overstate it: rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0, so the POL-NS-04(c) accuracy test cannot be run, and under POL-NS-11 that is neutral - it neither exonerates her nor impairs the driver's track, and it does not lower the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap on findings that rest on his trace.

The fee should be returned now rather than held. No escalation trigger fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09 limbs (c) and (d) do not apply, and every artifact I rely on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so limb (e) does not apply either. Escalation is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than refunding it, which is not a win for the rider. On the money: the fare_breakdown shows a 4.00 cancellation fee charged, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so a full refund of the contested $4.00 is what returns the rider to the position the policy requires.

claims.text: The trip was terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and the record contains no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission anywhere in it; the driver's own termination record therefore discloses none of the driver-side fault that limb (d) treats as fatal to the charge.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record: the rider's locating message was sent at 08:15:02 and the driver answered at 08:15:30, 28 seconds later, so limb (b)'s requirement that the driver have neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call fails, and the clause does not apply whatever the reply said.

The arrival marker is not shown to be false under POL-NS-05. That clause fires only where a fix puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or travelling at 15 km/h or more, at the arrival timestamp, and the derived arrival block records no such finding at 08:12:35; the same unfiltered trace closes to 37.94 m from the pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the trace affirms that the vehicle reached the pickup point's immediate vicinity rather than never arriving.

The zero in-geofence dwell in the derived arrival block is an accuracy-filter artifact and not a finding of position: POL-NS-02 discards fixes reporting horizontal accuracy worse than 25 m and declares such fixes evidence of neither presence nor absence, yet qualifying_fix_count is 0 and the longest qualifying run is 0 seconds on a trace whose nearest in-radius fix is 37.94 m from the pin; the shortfall the rider's refund route depends on therefore measures the device's reported accuracy, not the driver's absence from the kerb.

The platform's own record of this trip measures the wait served at 7.9 minutes, from the 08:12:35 arrival event to the 08:20:30 cancellation, against a free waiting period in force of 300 seconds (platform_policy.free_wait_sec); nothing in the record displaces that arrival marker under POL-NS-05, and POL-NS-06's refund route turns on an effective dwell below that minimum, which the platform's own measurement shows was served.

No anti-farming withholding applies. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below POL-NS-07's four-or-more limb, and 2 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 is 1.5 per cent, below the 8 per cent limb; these are the only two profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test and both fall short, so compensation is neither withheld nor escalatable on that ground.

Where the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 per cent of the net cancellation fee: the fare record's own money block computes driver_compensation of SGD 3.20 on the SGD 4.00 charged, being the STANDARD zone fee in force for this trip, and the fee is carried as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

POL-NS-03(i) is not made out on these facts: the rider's message named Exit A, which is the registered pickup point itself, and the driver's own message identified the kerb outside Exit A, while the trace's closest approach of 37.94 m places the vehicle inside the STANDARD arrival radius; there is no record of a driver who failed to move to the entrance the rider named, and the no-compensation outcome of that limb should not be visited on him.

EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, its admissibility status is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight is 0.0, so it can carry no fact, POL-NS-06(i)'s interval-accumulation route cannot be run at all, and the absence is itself citable — no record establishes any kerbside restriction or enforcement that would explain why a car could not hold at the pickup kerb.

If the judge is not prepared to hold the fee chargeable, the two admissible platform records cannot both be right about the same interval — EV-TRIP-00212 records an arrival at 08:12:35 and a wait of 7.9 minutes while EV-GPS-00212 computes 0 seconds of in-geofence dwell from a trace whose only in-radius fixes are excluded as non-probative — and on that reading the disputed fee should be held under POL-NS-09 pending human review rather than refunded on the exported trace alone.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

WHY THE FEE DOES NOT STAND. Under POL-NS-01 the fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold; the arrival and waiting conditions fail.

(1) Arrival — POL-NS-01(b) read through POL-NS-02. The driver is deemed to have arrived only where the gps_trace contains at least three consecutive fixes, each with reported horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. EV-GPS-00212 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, holds 93 fixes across the whole 08:05:10–08:20:30 window with 100% coverage and no gaps, and returns qualifying_fix_count 0 with a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds. There is no qualifying in-radius fix at any point, so POL-NS-02's own rule applies: the driver never arrived at the pickup point to the required standard and limb (b) fails. The driver's strongest point — that an unfiltered fix closes to 37.94 m, inside the 50 m radius — does not save the charge. That reading did not survive the 25 m accuracy filter, and POL-NS-02 provides that fixes worse than 25 m are count as evidence of neither presence nor absence while still directing that absent a qualifying in-radius fix the driver is not deemed to have arrived. The admissibility note itself says poor accuracy here is data, not a defect, and that the record simply cannot place the driver inside the geofence to POL-NS-02's standard; that is a policy failure, not an impairment discount.

(2) Waiting period — POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06. The free waiting period in force is 300 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which governs the 180-second default). The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds, a shortfall of 300 seconds. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver's 'arrived' tap, and POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed route is unavailable because arrival_marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. The 7.9-minute wait_time_min in the trip record is therefore the interval from the driver-pressed marker to cancellation and does not establish a served waiting period. POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full on this arithmetic alone. POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable: EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no traffic_advisory can be summed.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. The driver's POL-NS-01(d) point is accepted — EXCESSIVE_WAIT is one of the three recognised codes and there is no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission — but limb (d) is not the limb that fails. His POL-NS-05 point is rejected: the derived block records no finding that the driver was more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at 08:12:35, so the marker is not shown false, but the refund does not depend on that clause. His reading of the 0-second dwell as a mere accuracy artifact is rejected for the reason above. His POL-NS-03(i) point is accepted as far as it goes, but POL-NS-03 is not the operative route in either direction: it requires the driver stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and the trace shows no held position (run_count 0) with fixes reaching 1082.40 m and speeds up to 43.5 km/h, so it does not apply; its limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is in any case unavailable because registered_pickup_points is 1. The rider's POL-NS-03 framing is noted but unnecessary, since POL-NS-02 already decides. Both sides' POL-NS-04 points are accepted: the driver replied 28 seconds after the rider's 08:15:02 locating message, so that clause does not apply, and nothing turns on it. The rider's POL-NS-11 point is accepted: rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 makes her own track's accuracy test unrunnable and neutral, and it neither exonerates her nor impairs the driver's trace.

DRIVER COMPENSATION AND ESCALATION. No compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check was run and does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 against completed_trips_30d of 132 is 1.5% (below 8%) — but there is nothing to pay. Escalation does not apply: confidence 0.9 is above the 0.70 floor; no artifact relied on is impaired under POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d); the trip record's driver-pressed arrival marker is resolved, not contradicted, by POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-12; the profile counters give no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) trigger; and the deciding facts rest on complete weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty.

PAYMENT. The fare record shows a $4.00 cancellation fee CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00; the full $4.00 is returned. The monetary effect ($4.00) is at or below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00 and executes automatically. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the S$4.00 cancellation fee on trip TRP-00212 is refunded in full to the rider.

The fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. I accept limb (a) (an 'arrived' event exists) and limb (d) (the trip was terminated by the driver under EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three recognised codes, with no boarding event and no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission). Two limbs nonetheless fail.

Arrival (limb (b), read through POL-NS-02). The trip record carries a driver-pressed marker at 08:12:35, but platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed-arrival route does not apply, and POL-NS-01(c) measures the arrival and the waiting clock from the GPS, not from the tap. The driver's own 93-fix trace (EV-GPS-00212, COMPLETE, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps) returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds: there is no run of three consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius with reported accuracy of 25 m or better anywhere in the 08:05:10 to 08:20:30 window. The clause's stated result where a trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix is that the driver did not arrive, so limb (b) fails. POL-NS-03 does not displace that: it requires the driver to have held position for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and the trace records no held run at all (run_count 0), the vehicle averaging 294.05 m from the pin, reaching 1082.40 m, at speeds up to 43.5 km/h. On either reading the S$4.00 comes back to the rider — if the driver was near but not at the pin, POL-NS-03 still refunds the fee in full.

Waiting time (limb (c), read through POL-NS-06). The free waiting period in force is 300 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which governs over the 180-second default), and the effective in-geofence dwell measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix is 0 seconds — a 300-second shortfall. The driver's figure of 7.9 minutes (wait_time_min) is the interval from the arrival tap to the cancellation, which POL-NS-01(c) expressly does not use. Interval summing under POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT): its absence is itself citable, and nothing shows a kerbside restriction or enforcement that explains why a car could not hold at the pickup kerb. The shortfall refunds the fee in full.

I have weighed the driver's argument that the zero dwell is only an accuracy artifact and not a finding of position. The trace is COMPLETE and is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) — no sampling gap, 93 fixes across the window, rider_track present, no clock skew against the arrival event, and the chat and fare lines reconcile — so poor horizontal accuracy is data rather than a defect, and the clause's own aggregate test still runs and finds nothing qualifying. Because the trace is not impaired under POL-NS-08, POL-NS-09(e) is not engaged and the confidence cap remains at the artifacts' weight of 1.0. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the driver replied 28 seconds after her 08:15:02 message, so limb (b) fails and I do not use that clause. Driver compensation is nil. POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-10(g) does not apply, so POL-NS-07 pays nothing. (The anti-farming check would not have withheld it — 2 no-show terminations against 132 completed trips is 1.5 per cent — but no payout is due in any event.)

The full S$4.00 is returned; the monetary effect (S$4.00) is within the automatic-execution threshold. Confidence 0.90, capped at 1.00 by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the finding. No clause of the policy produces a referral on these facts.

To both parties. The rider's dispute is upheld: the $4.00 cancellation fee shown on EV-FARE-00212 (cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded in full.

Why the fee is not chargeable. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and the rider wins by breaking any one. The driver's termination record (EV-TRIP-00212) does satisfy limbs (a) and (d): there is an 'arrived' event at 08:12:35, and the trip was ended by the driver at 08:20:30 under EXCESSIVE_WAIT, a code limb (d) recognises. Limb (b) fails. POL-NS-02 deems the driver to have arrived only where the gps_trace contains at least three consecutive fixes, each reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. On EV-GPS-00212 the derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds across the whole 08:05:10 to 08:20:30 window. That trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and its own admissibility note says in terms that poor horizontal accuracy here is data rather than a defect and that the record cannot place the driver inside the geofence to the standard POL-NS-02 requires. That is a failure of the policy test, not a confidence discount. Fixes reporting worse than 25 m are counted as evidence of neither presence nor absence, so the unfiltered 37.94 m nearest approach on the driver's trace does not establish arrival. POL-NS-02 therefore decides it: no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere means the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund. The driver's contrary point (that his trace closes to 37.94 m, inside the 50 m radius) is met and rejected on that basis.

Independent ground. POL-NS-06 refunds in full on its own arithmetic. The free waiting period in force is 300 seconds (EV-TRIP-00212 platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which governs over the 180 second default); the measured effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec 0.0 over run_count 0), a shortfall of 300 seconds; and limb (i)'s interval summing cannot bridge it because EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING (status MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the accumulation route is simply unavailable. Both routes lead to the same full refund.

The driver's remaining points. (1) The reason code is valid — accepted — but a valid limb (d) does not carry the charge when limb (b) fails. (2) That POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider is accepted; both sides agree the driver replied 28 seconds after her locating message, so that clause does not apply, and the rider's refund rests on POL-NS-02 instead of POL-NS-04. (7) POL-NS-03 does not govern: it requires the driver stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, and his trace shows run_count 0 of held position, speeds to 43.5 km/h and a 3.2 km footprint, so that clause decides nothing here and no compensation flows from it. (8) The missing advisory carries no fact and is cited only for its absence — accepted. (9) Escalation is rejected. POL-NS-01(c) itself resolves the measurement question the driver says is a contradiction, so POL-NS-09(b) does not fire; the anti-farming limb (d) does not fire (2 of 132, 1.5%); limbs (c) and (e) do not fire; and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. Escalation is terminal and would hold the rider's money, which is not what this record supports.

Compensation. No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, which it is not; POL-NS-03 does not engage; and the pin-ambiguity goodwill of POL-NS-03(ii) is unavailable because registered_pickup_points is 1 and the rider did specify a sub-location.

Referrals. None. No clause that produces a referral fires: the marker is not established FALSE (POL-NS-05), the anti-farming packet (POL-NS-07) does not trip, and the reason code is EXCESSIVE_WAIT rather than a mis-selected DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE.

Evidence weight. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any fact relied on here; EV-GPS-00212 and EV-TRIP-00212 both carry weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on this ruling is 1.0 and the ruling stands on unimpaired evidence. Nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): there is no clock skew, no trace gap over 120 s, no chat defect (4 messages against chat_message_count 4, msg_id sequence intact, driver replied in 28 s) and the fare line reconciles with the fee in force. The only below-weight artifact is the MISSING advisory, which carries nothing.

The monetary effect is $4.00, below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this refund executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route.

The driver also cannot fall back on the platform-confirmed arrival route. POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO marker, and the marker in force on this trip is BUTTON - trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is 'BUTTON' - so the platform's arrival and wait-timer events cannot carry POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c). Because the arrival was driver-pressed, both his arrival and his dwell must be established from the exported trace under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05, and on that trace there is no qualifying in-radius fix and no qualifying stationary run.

The rider's refund does not depend on winning the 50 metre point. If the driver is treated as stationary near but not at the pin, POL-NS-03 still refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. His trace is not a kerbside wait: across the 15-minute window his fixes average 294.05 m from the pickup pin, reach 1082.40 m away, and record speeds up to 43.5 km/h over a 3.2 km trace, with run_count 0 of held position. So on either clause - POL-NS-02 or POL-NS-03 - the $4.00 goes back to the rider.

On the POL-NS-03 route the driver bears his own loss and receives nothing, under limb (i): the rider stated the correct entrance in the chat log - 'im at exit A, which car ah? i dont see anything here' at 08:15:02 - and 'Exit A' is the registered pickup point itself, 'Raffles Place MRT (Exit A)'. The driver replied at 08:15:30 and then cancelled at 08:20:30 without moving to her. Where the rider named the entrance and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, no compensation is payable.

The pin-ambiguity goodwill also fails on its own terms. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) requires both that neither party specified a sub-location and that trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2 or more. registered_pickup_points is 1, and the rider did specify a sub-location, so limb (ii) cannot be reached and the 50 percent goodwill is not available.

I concede that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and I do not run it as her route to the fee. Limb (a) is satisfied: her 08:15:02 message is locating on its face. But limb (b) fails, because the driver replied in the chat 28 seconds later at 08:15:30, which takes the case out of the clause regardless of what the reply said. The same message still does work under POL-NS-03(i): it shows she told him exactly where she was standing, and he cancelled anyway.

The rider's own device corroborates her account of standing at the kerb. Her track holds 60 fixes between 08:08:00 and 08:22:00, every one of them at 0.0 km/h, at distances of 2.18 m to 40.37 m from the pickup pin - inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius on the raw numbers. I do not overstate it: rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0, so the POL-NS-04(c) accuracy test cannot be run, and under POL-NS-11 that is neutral - it neither exonerates her nor impairs the driver's track, and it does not lower the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap on findings that rest on his trace.

The fee should be returned now rather than held. No escalation trigger fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09 limbs (c) and (d) do not apply, and every artifact I rely on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so limb (e) does not apply either. Escalation is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than refunding it, which is not a win for the rider. On the money: the fare_breakdown shows a 4.00 cancellation fee charged, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so a full refund of the contested $4.00 is what returns the rider to the position the policy requires.

The trip was terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code EXCESSIVE_WAIT, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and the record contains no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission anywhere in it; the driver's own termination record therefore discloses none of the driver-side fault that limb (d) treats as fatal to the charge.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record: the rider's locating message was sent at 08:15:02 and the driver answered at 08:15:30, 28 seconds later, so limb (b)'s requirement that the driver have neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call fails, and the clause does not apply whatever the reply said.

The arrival marker is not shown to be false under POL-NS-05. That clause fires only where a fix puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or travelling at 15 km/h or more, at the arrival timestamp, and the derived arrival block records no such finding at 08:12:35; the same unfiltered trace closes to 37.94 m from the pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the trace affirms that the vehicle reached the pickup point's immediate vicinity rather than never arriving.

The zero in-geofence dwell in the derived arrival block is an accuracy-filter artifact and not a finding of position: POL-NS-02 discards fixes reporting horizontal accuracy worse than 25 m and declares such fixes evidence of neither presence nor absence, yet qualifying_fix_count is 0 and the longest qualifying run is 0 seconds on a trace whose nearest in-radius fix is 37.94 m from the pin; the shortfall the rider's refund route depends on therefore measures the device's reported accuracy, not the driver's absence from the kerb.

The platform's own record of this trip measures the wait served at 7.9 minutes, from the 08:12:35 arrival event to the 08:20:30 cancellation, against a free waiting period in force of 300 seconds (platform_policy.free_wait_sec); nothing in the record displaces that arrival marker under POL-NS-05, and POL-NS-06's refund route turns on an effective dwell below that minimum, which the platform's own measurement shows was served.

No anti-farming withholding applies. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below POL-NS-07's four-or-more limb, and 2 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 132 is 1.5 per cent, below the 8 per cent limb; these are the only two profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test and both fall short, so compensation is neither withheld nor escalatable on that ground.

Where the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 per cent of the net cancellation fee: the fare record's own money block computes driver_compensation of SGD 3.20 on the SGD 4.00 charged, being the STANDARD zone fee in force for this trip, and the fee is carried as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

POL-NS-03(i) is not made out on these facts: the rider's message named Exit A, which is the registered pickup point itself, and the driver's own message identified the kerb outside Exit A, while the trace's closest approach of 37.94 m places the vehicle inside the STANDARD arrival radius; there is no record of a driver who failed to move to the entrance the rider named, and the no-compensation outcome of that limb should not be visited on him.

EV-ADVIS-00212-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, its admissibility status is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight is 0.0, so it can carry no fact, POL-NS-06(i)'s interval-accumulation route cannot be run at all, and the absence is itself citable — no record establishes any kerbside restriction or enforcement that would explain why a car could not hold at the pickup kerb.

If the judge is not prepared to hold the fee chargeable, the two admissible platform records cannot both be right about the same interval — EV-TRIP-00212 records an arrival at 08:12:35 and a wait of 7.9 minutes while EV-GPS-00212 computes 0 seconds of in-geofence dwell from a trace whose only in-radius fixes are excluded as non-probative — and on that reading the disputed fee should be held under POL-NS-09 pending human review rather than refunded on the exported trace alone.
